av_event.what: Before answering, Graham goes silent for about five seconds. He looks down and away to his right towards the window, lets out an audible slow breath through his nose and rubs his jaw with one hand, then looks back just below the camera and speaks.

text:
A: Afternoon! Gary. Can you hear me alright, mate?
B: Yeah. Graham.
A: Graham, good stuff. Where are you, then? I'm guessing local from the calendar behind you. That's a Baggies calendar, yeah?
B: Tipton.
A: Tipton! I'm Aldridge, so we're practically neighbours. I'm Walsall born and bred though, so I won't hold the Albion against you.
B: Ar. Saddlers.
A: Afraid so, mate. Suffering for it, too. Saturday was shocking. We couldn't hit a barn door. You see the Baggies?
B: On the radio. Draw. Should have won it.
A: That's football, isn't it. You still go?
B: Not now. Had a season ticket in me forties. Knees are bad now, the steps and that.
A: Fair enough. I get to Villa Park now and again, corporate box, supplier pays, you know how it is. Not complaining. Sorry, I should've said, I'm in sales. Fixings and fasteners, industrial stuff. Out on the road most of the week. M6 was a car park this morning round junction 10. Took me forty minutes to get past Walsall, couldn't believe it. Still, the car's comfy, that's the main thing. Got the 5 Series, so I just sit there with the radio. What line were you in, Graham?
B: Toolmaker. Then maintenance fitter.
A: Proper trade, that. Whereabouts?
B: Round here. Tipton, Wednesbury, Oldbury. Small firms. Most of them have gone now.
A: Yeah, that's the Black Country, isn't it. Half my old customers have shut up shop. The ones that are left are good firms, mind. Toolmaker, you'll know what an anchor bolt's meant to look like better than half the buyers I deal with.
B: Probably, yeah.
A: You retired now?
B: Three year. Bit more.
A: Lovely. I'm aiming for sixty, mortgage cleared, place in Spain maybe. What do you do with yourself, then? Bet the days fly by.
B: Er... not really. Shed, mostly. Got a lawnmower engine in bits. Two year it's been in bits.
A: Ha! Two years! That's commitment, mate.
B: Sandra says I'll be buried with it.
A: Sandra's your missus? Mine's Karen. She'd say the same about my golf. Sunday mornings, every week, same three lads, out Sutton Coldfield way. I'm about fourteen on a good day. You play?
B: No. Played Sunday league, years back. Football.
A: Oh, did you? What position?
B: Centre half. Pub team. Weren't much good, to be honest.
A: Centre half, I'd have guessed that. You've got the look of a man who'd put you in the stand. Grandkids, are they, in the photo?
B: Yeah. Our son's two. There's three altogether. They come Sundays.
A: That's nice, that. Mine are grown up. No grandkids yet, thank God, I'm too young. Lad's in Lichfield, and our daughter's at Nottingham Trent, final year. First in the family to go, actually. Anyway. Do you do the Sunday dinner then, big family do?
B: Sandra does it. I carve.
A: Ha, that's the important job. Same as me with the barbecue. Stand there with a lager, take the credit.
B: Ar.
A: Listen, I reckon we're about done. Good to meet you, Graham. Up the Saddlers, eh?
B: Ar. Tara.
A: Tara, mate.
